### VII. Main Section §. 54.

Whoever has read some books of the Holy Fathers, and in particular such in which truths of faith are dealt with, cannot make this draft. I suspect it only among those who know nothing else than their schoolbooks. These I ask to answer a question: Is the teaching of the Holy Fathers without distinction also the teaching of the universal Church? If they answer yes: then I will convict them that the universal Church contradicts itself. I can bring forward propositions which are not accepted by the Church, but are taught by just as many, partly even more Church Fathers, than can be brought forward for the explanation of our prophecy. If they answer no: then I ask further: What does one have for a characteristic mark to distinguish in the writings of the Holy Fathers their teaching from the teaching of the universal Church? It cannot depend on the judgment of theologians: otherwise the sense of the Church would be tested not from the Holy Fathers, but from the pronouncement of living scholars. One must not seek the difference in the matter itself, whether it concerns the faith or not: because it is still doubtful, and it shall first be shown from the Fathers that a proposition, for example, that Isaiah prophesied of Christ in the seventh chapter, is a point of faith. The characteristic mark must be sought and shown in the writings themselves. The true one is if the Holy Father explicitly says: he does not assert it from his own sense, but he believes it: the opposite opinion is contrary to the general faith: let no one doubt it who confesses the general faith: that is what we have learned from Christ and the Apostles.

<summary>The author challenges the idea that all writings of the Fathers represent official Church doctrine, highlighting the need for explicit markers of "universal faith."</summary>
<keywords>Church Fathers, universal Church, doctrine, theologians, Isaiah, faith, Apostles</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the Parable of the Talents and the unequal distribution of divine gifts. It concludes the sentence from the previous page regarding the "ear-tugging" reminder to be diligent, transitioning into a series of natural analogies—gems, plants, and stars—to justify why human souls and bodies possess varying degrees of excellence and glory.</meta>

-># ON THE SECRETS OF NATURE<-

...industry, but to keep watch continuously and to persist with tireless labor in the business <note>original: "nundinationi," literally referring to trading at a market, used here as a metaphor for spiritual work</note> of salvation, saying: "Trade <margin>Luke 19</margin> until I come." When Paul, the chosen instrument <note>original: "organum electionis," a traditional title for St. Paul derived from Acts 9:15</note>, diligently impressed this upon others, he himself strove to fulfill it in every way, so that in the mission committed to him he was more fervent than others, and more eager and vivid in performing the duties of his Apostolic office.

<margin>A Simile</margin> Just as there is a distinction in gems, living creatures, herbs, and stars—and one flower is more fragrant than another, and one gem more glittering—so it happens in the souls of men; for they are equipped with a certain peculiar power and faculty, and they produce various operations and diverse effects. <margin>Simile. 1 Cor. 15</margin> For just as (as Paul says) a power is implanted in each seed, and the flesh of beasts is one thing, that of men another, and as there is one kind of beauty and grace for celestial bodies and another for earthly ones—one brightness for the Sun, another for the Moon, and another splendor for the stars—so one human body is more excellent than another, and of a more noble character. 

And the soul itself—both in this current station and in the course of this life, as well as in the resurrection—is more powerful in its dignity and condition, and superior in glory, according to its lot and merits. Indeed, there is a great disparity and unlikeness, and a very different condition, between the upright and the wicked, both in the present age and in the one to come. For the ungodly in the mid[st]...

<summary>This page argues that human diversity in talent and character is a natural reflection of the variety found in the physical world, such as the differing brilliance of stars or fragrance of flowers. It concludes that these natural differences persist into the afterlife, where the souls of the righteous will possess greater glory than others.</summary>

<keywords>St. Paul, Luke 19, 1 Corinthians 15, resurrection, spiritual industry, natural hierarchy, celestial bodies, human diversity</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the "Internal Support" strategy for treating sores and ulcers. The previous page established that tonifying the body is essential for pushing toxins outward and that treatment should begin before the wound even opens. This section focuses on specific herbal modifications for complications and distinguishes between the physical presentation of Yang-type and Yin-type ulcers.</meta>

If **Cinnamon bark** <note>original: 肉桂 (ròu-guì)</note> is used heavily, but there is itching and pain caused by **wind** <note>In Chinese medicine, "wind" (fēng) often refers to symptoms that move quickly or cause itching</note>, add **Saposhnikovia root** <note>original: 防風 (fáng-fēng)</note> and **Gastrodia rhizome** <note>original: 天麻 (tiān-má)</note>. If the flesh has become **necrotic** <gloss>dead or non-healing tissue</gloss>, add **Pubescent Angelica root** <note>original: 獨活 (dú-huó)</note> and **Cassia bark** <note>original: 官桂 (guān-guì)</note>.

For cases of extreme pain, add **Myrrh** <note>original: 沒藥 (mò-yào)</note> and **Frankincense** <note>original: 乳香 (rǔ-xiāng)</note>. These are all modified methods for treating the variations of **Yang syndromes** <note>Acute, red, and hot conditions</note>. 

However, if a **Yin eruption** <note>Deep-seated, cold-type sores that do not easily surface</note> transforms into a state of **deficiency and mental confusion** <note>original: 虛愦 (xū-kuì) — a state of physical exhaustion and delirium</note>, one must use large doses of **Ginseng** <note>original: 人參 (rén-shēn)</note>, **Astragalus**, and **Atractylodes** <note>original: 芪朮 (qí-zhú) — two primary herbs for boosting energy and the immune system</note>. To these, add plenty of **Honeysuckle flower** <note>original: 金銀花 (jīn-yín-huā)</note>, **Cinnamon bark**, **Aconite** <note>original: 附子 (fù-zǐ) — a potent warming herb</note>, and the like. By doing so, one may stabilize these extraordinary transformations. One must absolutely never stubbornly adhere to Yang syndrome treatment methods when attempting to treat the transformations of a **Yin-type ulcer**.

### Discourse on the Opening of Sores and Ulcers

In a **Yang-type sore**, once the pus has formed, it will certainly be pointed, firm, and **protruding** <note>original: 突出 (tū-chū)</note>. If a blade is used to open its head, the **pus and blood** <note>original: 膿血 (nóng-xuè)</note> will gush forth; once the opening is drained, the condition will immediately improve. It will certainly not spread further or rot without end. 

However, there are certain types of sores that do **not protrude significantly** <note>original: 突起 (tū-qǐ)</note>, though there is swelling and pain. The pain may be heavy or light. In light cases, there is **numbness and a lack of sensation** <gloss>the patient cannot feel the area</gloss>. If such a sore occurs on the back, it feels as heavy as a mountain. In severe cases, the sensation is exactly like being cut, pierced, or stabbed with a knife. After five to seven days, a head may emerge from the top...

<summary>This page provides specific herbal modifications for post-ulceration complications and emphasizes that Yin-type ulcers (characterized by numbness or deep-seated pain) must be treated with warming tonics rather than standard cooling methods used for Yang-type sores.</summary>
<keywords>Yang syndrome, Yin transformation, Internal Support (Netuo), Cinnamon bark, Ginseng, Suppuration, Necrotic tissue, Herbal modifications</keywords>

translation:
# Kohut’s Place in American Judaism

This is the year in which we of the progressive school have been celebrating the centenary of Isaac M. Wise, the virtual father of American Reform. None the less, our survey of Judaism as a whole should be sufficiently comprehensive to realize the value of Kohut's contribution to the cause in making for a more positive Judaism. Let us not forget that Dr. Wise was a staunch pleader for the sanctity of Bible law, and that his views would be classed as conservative today. Dr. Kohut, then, prepared the way for that genius, Solomon Schechter, who "came and saw and conquered." But that is another story.

If he were alive today, he would see a different line of cleavage. There are two camps still, but no longer those of Orthodoxy and Reform, but of Zionism on the one hand and anti-Nationalism on the other. We are not as keen as were our fathers as to the discriminating points of distinction in synagogue observance—as to the covered head in worship, the recital of prayer in Hebrew—the retention of some Orientalisms. We realize that "life fulfills itself in many ways." The vital question is, Which school makes for the best kind of Jew? Something can be said for both wings. The motive behind the action is everything. There is all the ethical difference in the world between ceasing to observe dietary laws because they are regarded as part of an ancient taboo, no longer accepted, or dropping them

He who otherwise prays this Psalm with reverence will be generally received with great favor.

**Psalm 16.**—This Psalm is important and can be profitably employed in different undertakings. As for example, 1st, If any one has been robbed, and wishes to know the name of the robber, he must proceed as follows: Take mud or slime and sand out of a stream, mix them together; then write the names of all suspected persons upon small slips of paper and apply the mixture on the reverse side of the slips; afterward lay them in a large and clean basin, filled for this purpose with fresh water from the stream—lay them in the water one by one, and at the same time pray this Psalm over them ten times with the prayer adapted to it keeping in mind at the same time the name of Caar, that is, Living, which name is found in the words of the sixth verse, as follows: Chabalim, and Alei, and if the name of the real thief is written upon the slips, that upon which his name is written will rise to the surface. The prayer is as follows: 
> Let it be thy will, Eel Caar, the Living God to make known the name of the thief, who stole from me (here name that which was stolen). Grant that the name of the thief, if it is among the names, may arise before thy eyes, and thus be made known to mine and all others who are present, that thy name may be glorified: grant it for the sake of thy holy name. Amen.—Selah!

2. Whoever prays this Psalm daily with reverence, and childlike trust upon the eternal love and goodness of God, directed to circumstances, will have all his sorrows changed into joy.
Finally, it is said, that the daily praying of this Psalm will change enemies into friends, and will disperse all pain and sorrow.

**Psalm 17.**—A traveler, who prays this Psalm early in the morning, with ardor, together with the proper prayer, in the name of Jah, will be secure from all evil for twenty-four hours. The prayer is as follows: 
> May it be thy holy will, Oh, Jah, Jenora, to make my journey prosperous, to lead me in pleasant paths, to protect me from all evil, and to bring me safely back to my loved ones, for thy mighty and adorable name’s sake. Amen.

The two letters of the holy name Jah are taken from the words, Shoddini, verse 9, and Mirmah, verse 1.

**Psalm 18.**—If robbers are about to attack you, pray this Psalm quickly but frevently, with the prayer belonging to it, with confidence in the holiest name of Eel Jah, that is, mighty, all-merciful and compassionate God, the robbers will leave you suddenly, without inflicting the slightest injury upon you. The letters necessary to make the holy name of God are contained in the words, Aisher, verse 1; Shoal, verse 1; Tamin, verse 33, and Haol, verse 47.
The prayer is the following: 
> “Mighty, all-merciful and compassionate God, Eel Jah! may it be pleasing to thy most holy will, to defend me against approaching robbers, and protect me against all enemies, opposers and evil circumstances, for thine is the power and thou canst help. Hear me for the sake of thy most holy name, Eel Jah. Amen.—Selah!

Afterward, lay them in a large and clean basin, filled for this purpose with fresh water from the stream. Lay them in the water one by one, and at the same time, pray this Psalm over them ten times with the prayer adapted to it, keeping in mind at the same time the name of *Caar* (that is, "Living"), which name is found in the words of the sixth verse: *Chabalim* and *Alei*. If the name of the real thief is written upon the slips, that one upon which his name is written will rise to the surface. The prayer is as follows: 
->Let it be thy will, *Eel Caar*, the Living God, to make known the name of the thief who stole from me (here name that which was stolen). Grant that the name of the thief, if it is among the names, may arise before thy eyes and thus be made known to mine and all others who are present, that thy name may be glorified; grant it for the sake of thy holy name. Amen. — Selah!<-

2. Whoever prays this Psalm daily with reverence and childlike trust upon the eternal love and goodness of God, directed to his circumstances, will have all his sorrows changed into joy. 
Finally, it is said that the daily praying of this Psalm will change enemies into friends and will disperse all pain and sorrow.

**Psalm 17.**—A traveler who prays this Psalm early in the morning with ardor, together with the proper prayer in the name of *Jah*, will be secure from all evil for twenty-four hours. The prayer is as follows: 
->May it be thy holy will, Oh, *Jah*, *Jenora*, to make my journey prosperous, to lead me in pleasant paths, to protect me from all evil, and to bring me safely back to my loved ones, for thy mighty and adorable name’s sake. Amen.<-

The two letters of the holy name *Jah* are taken from the words *Shoddini* (verse 9) and *Mirmah* (verse 1).

**Psalm 18.**—If robbers are about to attack you, pray this Psalm quickly but fervently, with the prayer belonging to it, with confidence in the holiest name of *Eel Jah* (that is, "mighty, all-merciful, and compassionate God"). The robbers will leave you suddenly without inflicting the slightest injury upon you. The letters necessary to make the holy name of God are contained in the words *Aisher* (verse 1), *Shoal* (verse 1), *Tamin* (verse 33), and *Haol* (verse 47).
The prayer is the following: 
->“Mighty, all-merciful, and compassionate God, *Eel Jah*! May it be pleasing to thy most holy will to defend me against approaching robbers and protect me against all enemies, opposers, and evil circumstances, for thine is the power and thou canst help. Hear me for the sake of thy most holy name, *Eel Jah*. Amen. — Selah!”<-

<summary>This page outlines rituals for detecting thieves via water divination (Psalm 16) and obtaining protection for travelers and against robbers (Psalms 17 and 18).</summary>

that gladdens the earth and the air and the sea

More perfect than any other figure

has no principle or end to its measure.
This is an eternal similitude.

to all things it gives generation,
beginning and end, and various condition.

how there is one God in three persons,
distinct and each one singular,
not mixed but with perfect union.

and one is not after nor before the other.

that mirror generates the splendor,

proceeds the heat,
and there will never be nor was there

immediately He does His works.

As you look from the grand entrance toward the altar, the side posts <note>original: "jambs"</note> of the two nearest <note>original: "hithermost"</note> *Trilithons* present themselves with a magnificent opening 25 cubits wide <note>A cubit is an ancient unit of measurement, approximately 20.8 inches</note>. One remarkable detail in the construction of this oval is that the two nearest *Trilithons* that correspond to one another—that is, those next to the grand entrance on the right hand and the left—are exceeded in height by the next two in order. Their height is unequal, much like that of the *Trilithons*, rising higher toward the upper end of the <term>Adytum</term> <note>The innermost, most sacred part of a temple</note>. <vocab>Pausanias, Antoninus, Graecia, Arcadia, Megalopolis, Pallantium, Tegea, Romaei, Germani, Sauromatae</vocab>
translation:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>a violent earthquake fell upon them; but Emperor Antoninus restored even these through excessive expenditure and eagerness for their rebuilding. Now as to all his gifts of money both to Greeks and to those barbarians who requested them, and the construction of public works in Greece, throughout Ionia, around Carthage, and in the land of the Syrians, others have recorded these things with the greatest accuracy. But this emperor left behind also another deed worthy of memory. As many of his subjects as were Roman citizens, while their children were reckoned as Greeks, these parents were faced with either distributing their property to those unrelated to them or augmenting the emperor's wealth according to a certain law; Antoninus, however, permitted even these citizens to bestow the inheritance upon their own children, preferring to appear benevolent rather than to uphold a law profitable in terms of money. The Romans called this emperor <term>Pius</term> <gloss>Dutiful or Pious</gloss>, because he was seen especially to practice honour toward the divine; in my judgment he might also bear the title of Cyrus the elder, being called the Father of Mankind. He also left behind to inherit the empire a son of the same name; and this second Antoninus <note>Marcus Aurelius, adopted son and successor of Antoninus Pius</note> went out to take vengeance upon the Germans, the most warlike and numerous of the barbarians in Europe, and also the nation of the Sauromatae <note>Sarmatians</note>, who had initiated war and wrongdoing.

The remaining portion of our Arcadian account: there is a road leading out from Megalopolis to Pallantium and to Tegea, which runs as far as the place called the Dyke <note>Choma</note>.
